widgets.title: Fraud detection & investigation
widgets.description: A bank's payments are scored by its own fraud model. An AI agent built with the NeMo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA Nemotron investigates every alert inside an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox. It opens cases; only the analyst confirms a case or blocks an account. Customer data never leaves the bank.

widgets.title: The architecture
widgets.description: Fraud Detection & Investigation is a Blueprint in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA. The Studio shows what it is made of.

annotations.text: The architecture of **Fraud Detection & Investigation**, as the Studio draws it: the agent in its **NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox**, the systems it works with, the shared **NVIDIA** models and the people who decide. Green lines are allowed, red ones refused by the sandbox's policy.
The **agent**: a NeMo Agent Toolkit agent, packaged as one component of the Blueprint. Its sandbox, providers and policy deploy with it.
It reasons with an **NVIDIA NIM** shared by every use case from the *NVIDIA Models (shared)* Blueprint: downloaded once, always up.
Everything else is **outside**: the sandbox refuses it. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

widgets.title: The use case at work
widgets.description: The use case's own page, step by step: what the agent does, and what it is not allowed to do.

annotations.text: The use case's own page: the Blueprint is **ready** in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA and the agent's sandbox is up. The log on the right is OpenShell's: every request the agent makes, allowed or denied.
Step by step. First, **score every payment**.
The bank's fraud model runs **inside the agent's sandbox**: the sandbox is the bank's data boundary, written as policy. **Run it here**.
About 1,500 payments scored in a fraction of a second; the risky ones are above the threshold.
Next: why was a payment flagged, and why wasn't another?
A score alone doesn't help the analyst. **SHAP** explains each alert.
A new device, tiny test charges, money passed on within the hour: the reasons behind each alert.
And the traveller in Lisbon?
Not flagged: there is a travel notice on file. Fewer false alarms for the analyst.
Now the agent works the alerts on its own.
A **NeMo Agent Toolkit** agent on **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning** plans and calls the tools: it reads each case, screens payees against the sanctions list, and opens one case per pattern.
The cases it opened, each waiting for the analyst's review. Every tool call shows up in the OpenShell log, allowed.
Can the agent block the account itself?
Let it try: the agent asks core banking to block the account.
**403, policy denied.** NVIDIA OpenShell refuses the request before the bank ever sees it: enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.
The report, and the data boundary.
The agent files the **daily fraud report** in core banking.
The report: the cases, the money at risk, and the decisions left to the analyst.
Last: can the agent reach the internet?
**Blocked**, every time, and logged in red. The bank's data stays on the customer's own infrastructure.
